questions.text: What happens if, during a cycle, another module reads an export let or export const before its initializer?
options: ReferenceError. The binding exists, but it stays in the TDZ until initialization
It returns undefined, as with var
It returns the value that will be assigned later
A SyntaxError while the file is parsed

questions.text: What does export * leave out?
options: The default export. It is re-exported with a separate entry, such as export { default } from

questions.text: Why can another module already see an export function during a cycle, while the bodies are still starting?
options: The function is copied onto the global object
Cycles are forbidden, and 0 is substituted for the function
The function declaration initializes the binding before the bodies run
export function behaves like var and starts as undefined

questions.text: How does an early read of export var in a cycle differ from export let?
options: Both return the value that was assigned
var throws ReferenceError, let returns undefined
var already holds undefined. let is still in the TDZ, and the read throws ReferenceError

questions.text: If the same name arrives from two export * and there is no explicit export of that name, a static import { name } from that module fails.
A module namespace object can be given an own property.
If evaluating a module threw, the next import of the same URL runs the body again.
The argument of import() must be a string literal, like a static import specifier.
How do you re-export default when export * does not carry it?
questions.answer: export { default } from '...' or export { default as name } from '...'.

questions.text: How do you read default with a named import?
questions.answer: import { default as name } from '...'. The importer chooses the local name.

questions.text: What is the [[Prototype]] of a module namespace object?
questions.answer: null. It does not inherit Object.prototype.

questions.text: How do you resolve the clash when two export * export the same name?
questions.answer: With an explicit re-export of that name, such as export { n } from './a.mjs'. That export wins over the star clash.
